dct_description_sm: A baseline fishery, aquatic invertebrate, and plankton study was conducted during the summer of 1977 in the vicinity of Imperial Oil dredging operations at Tuft Point, NWT. Tuft Point coastal waters support a relatively abundant and diverse fish fauna (16 species). The region is of particular importance as a rearing area for the juveniles of anadromous species such as ciscoes, whitefish, and inconnu.   As part of the Imperial Oil Limited this project aimed at: 1) to determine the species composition and relative abundance of fish within the study area; 2) to identify important fish habitat zones; 3) to determine species composition, standing crop, and diversity of benthic macroinvertebrate and plankton communities; 4) to determine the food habits of the fish species present in the study area; 5) to conduct basic life history analyses of the major species presen;t 6) to use the baseline data thus obtained to: a) assess the effects of present and future Imperial Oil borrow operations upon fish populations in the area; b) form the basis for recommendations to mitigate any effects and for guidelines to be used in planning future borrow sites.
dct_title_s: Fish, aquatic invertebrates and plankton during the summer 1977 at Tuft Point, N.W.T.
